newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU delay could sabotage project - Deutsche analyst.
newsitem.headline: EMU delay could sabotage project - Deutsche analyst.

text.p: Any delay to the 1999 start-date for a single European currency could sabotage the whole project, a German analyst said on Thursday.
But Norbert Walter, chief economist at Deutsche Bank, told German radio that even Germany will find it hard to fulfil the necessary entry criteria.
"Anyone who plans to delay the start of EMU is sabotaging the whole currency union," said Walter.
Germany will find it "very difficult" to meet criteria laid out in the Maastricht Treaty for entry into European economic and monetary union.
"This is because Germany is virtually in a recession," Walter said.

He said any attempts to delay EMU would scupper recent efforts by would-be members to introduce measures of fiscal discipline aimed at meeting entry criteria. "It would tear the whole project apart," Walter said.
Should Germany fall just short of the criteria, it was not catastrophic as the treaty said countries moving in the right direction to fulfilling the criteria could also take part.

Walter said the situation in Britain was better than in Germany. Britain had done its economic homework and was now seeing falling unemployment and higher economic growth, while practically the opposite was true in Germany.
The issues of doing away with subsidies, pension reform and reform of the tax law in Germany had not been properly dealt with up to now, Walter said.
